summary: Shows kinit -f and klist -f to confirm a forwardable ticket (F flag), and setting GSSAPIDelegateCredentials=yes in ~/.ssh/config or ansible_ssh_common_args. Unlike psrp or winrm, the SSH plugin can't get a Kerberos ticket from a username and password, so you need a valid ticket before running.
questions: How do I check my Kerberos ticket is forwardable?
Where do I set GSSAPIDelegateCredentials for Ansible?
Can the SSH connection plugin get a Kerberos ticket from ansible_password?
Why does Kerberos over SSH fail even though I set a password?

answer_card.title: Kerberos delegation over SSH to Windows
answer_card.answer_md:
Get and check a forwardable ticket; look for `F` in the flags:

```bash
kinit -f username@REALM.COM
klist -f
# ... Flags: FRIA
```

Set delegation in `~/.ssh/config` or as an inventory hostvar:

```yaml+jinja
ansible_ssh_common_args: -o GSSAPIDelegateCredentials=yes
```

Unlike `psrp` and `winrm`, the SSH plugin **can't** get a Kerberos TGT from an explicit username and password, so you must have a valid ticket before running the playbook.
